title.zh: 卷一百八十七 志第一百四十 兵一
title.raw: 卷一百八十七 志第一百四十 兵一 Volume 187 Treatises 140: Military 1

sentences.zh: 禁軍上

translations.literal: Palace Guards, Part One
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Guards, Part One

sentences.zh: 宋之兵制，大概有三：天子之衛兵，以守京師，備征戍，曰禁軍；

translations.literal: The military system of Song, in broad outline, had three kinds: the emperor's guard troops, to defend the capital, prepare for campaigns and garrison duty—called the Palace Army;
translations.idiomatic: Song military organization fell broadly into three categories: the emperor's personal guard, stationed at the capital for defense and ready for campaign or frontier service—the Palace Army;

sentences.zh: 諸州之鎮兵，以分給役使，曰廂軍；

translations.literal: the garrison troops of the various prefectures, assigned to distribute labor and service—called the Garrison Army;
translations.idiomatic: prefectural garrison forces assigned to local labor and duties—the Garrison Army;

sentences.zh: 選於戶籍或應募，使之團結訓練，以爲在所防守，則曰鄉兵。

translations.literal: those selected from household registers or by recruitment, made to unite and train for local defense where they were stationed—were called Militia.
translations.idiomatic: men drawn from household registers or by recruitment, organized and trained for local defense where they served—the Militia.

sentences.zh: 又有蕃兵，其法始于國初，具籍塞下，團結以爲藩籬之兵；

translations.literal: There were also tribal frontier troops; the method began at the founding of the dynasty, registering them below the passes and uniting them as barrier troops;
translations.idiomatic: There were also tribal frontier forces. The practice dated to the dynasty's founding: men along the border passes were registered and organized as a defensive screen.

sentences.zh: 其後分隊伍，給旗幟，繕營堡，備器械，一律以鄉兵之制。

translations.literal: Later they were divided into units, given banners and flags, repaired fortresses and camps, equipped with weapons—all uniformly under the militia system.
translations.idiomatic: Later they were divided into units, issued banners, fortified camps, and supplied with arms—all on the same model as the militia.

sentences.zh: 今因舊史纂修《兵志》，特置於熙寧保甲之前，而附之鄉兵焉。

translations.literal: Now, compiling the Military Treatises from the old histories, they are specially placed before the Xining era baojia system and attached to the militia section.
translations.idiomatic: In compiling this Military Treatise from earlier histories, we place the tribal forces before the Xining-era baojia reforms and group them with the militia.

sentences.zh: 其軍政，則有召募、揀選、廩給、訓練、屯戍、遷補、器甲、馬政八者之目，條分而著之，以見歷朝因革損益之不同，而世道之盛衰亦具是矣。

translations.literal: As for military administration, there are eight categories: recruitment, selection, rations and pay, training, garrison and frontier service, promotion and replacement, arms and armor, and horse administration—each set forth in detail to show how successive reigns differed in reform, reduction, and increase, and how the rise and fall of the age is likewise embodied therein.
translations.idiomatic: Military administration is treated under eight headings—recruitment, selection, rations, training, garrison duty, promotion, arms and armor, and horse policy—each set out in detail so that changes from reign to reign may be seen, and with them the waxing and waning of the times.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 三代遠矣。

translations.literal: The Three Dynasties are far away.
translations.idiomatic: The age of the Three Dynasties lies far behind us.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢而下得寓兵于農之遺意者，惟唐府衛爲近之。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han downward, only the Tang fubing system came near to preserving the legacy of embedding soldiers among farmers.
translations.idiomatic: From Qin and Han onward, only the Tang fubing system came close to the old ideal of farmer-soldiers.

sentences.zh: 府衛變而召募，因循姑息，至於藩鎮盛而唐以亡。

translations.literal: When the fubing changed to recruitment, indulgence bred complacency, until the military governors grew powerful and Tang perished.
translations.idiomatic: When the fubing gave way to hired armies and indulgent neglect, the military governors grew strong—and Tang fell.

sentences.zh: 更曆五代，亂亡相踵，未有不由於兵者。

translations.literal: Through the Five Dynasties in turn, disorder and ruin followed one upon another—none without the cause of arms.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Five Dynasties, chaos and collapse followed in unbroken succession—always through the misuse of military power.

sentences.zh: 太祖起戎行，有天下，收四方勁兵，列營京畿，以備宿衛，分番屯戍，以捍邊圉。

translations.literal: Taizu rose from the army, gained the realm, gathered elite troops from the four quarters, arrayed camps in the capital region for palace guard duty, and rotated garrisons on the frontier to defend the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu rose from military life to win the empire. He gathered the best troops from every region, encamped them around the capital as the imperial guard, and rotated detachments to the frontier to hold the borders.

sentences.zh: 于時將帥之臣入奉朝請，獷暴之民收隸尺籍，雖有桀驁恣肆，而無所施於其間。

translations.literal: At that time generals and commanders came to court to attend audience; violent and fierce men were enrolled in the registers—though some were proud and unrestrained, they had nowhere to act out.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders then attended court in person; unruly men were brought under the rolls. Even the proud and violent had no room to act.

sentences.zh: 凡其制，爲什長之法，階級之辨，使之內外相維，上下相制，截然而不可犯者，是雖以矯累朝藩鎮之弊，而其所懲者深矣。

translations.literal: As for the system in general: the method of squad leaders, distinctions of rank, making inner and outer mutually sustain, upper and lower mutually restrain—so sharply that none could violate it—though this corrected the evils of military governors through successive reigns, what it punished ran deep.
translations.idiomatic: The system relied on squad leaders, clear ranks, and mutual checks between inner and outer, superior and subordinate—so tight that no one could break it. This corrected centuries of military-governor abuse, but the lesson it taught ran deep.

sentences.zh: 咸平以後，承平既久，武備漸寬。

translations.literal: After the Xianping era, long peace had been secured and military preparedness gradually relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xianping era, prolonged peace led military readiness to slacken.

sentences.zh: 仁宗之世，西兵招刺太多，將驕士惰，徒耗國用，憂世之士屢以爲言，竟莫之改。

translations.literal: In the reign of Renzong, too many western troops were recruited; generals grew arrogant and soldiers lazy, merely draining state revenue. Men concerned for the age spoke of it repeatedly, yet nothing was ever changed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Renzong, excessive recruitment for the western campaigns made generals arrogant and soldiers idle, draining the treasury. Critics spoke out again and again, but nothing changed.

sentences.zh: 神宗奮然更制，於是聯比其民以爲保甲，部分諸路以隸將兵，雖不能盡拯其弊，而亦足以作一時之氣。

translations.literal: Shenzong vigorously reformed the system; then the people were linked in baojia units, circuits were divided to attach to general-command troops—though the abuses could not all be saved, it was enough to rouse the spirit of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong boldly reformed the system, organizing the people into baojia units and restructuring circuit commands. The reforms could not cure every ill, but they restored morale for a time.

sentences.zh: 時其所任者，王安石也。

translations.literal: At that time the one entrusted was Wang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: The man entrusted with this was Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 元祐、紹聖遵守成憲。

translations.literal: Under Yuanyou and Shaosheng they observed the established statutes.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanyou and Shaosheng reigns simply followed established practice.

sentences.zh: 迨崇甯、大觀間，增額日廣而乏精銳，故無益于靖康之變。

translations.literal: By the Chongning and Daguan periods, quotas grew daily broader yet lacked elite troops; thus they were of no benefit at the Jingkang crisis.
translations.idiomatic: By the Chongning and Daguan eras, quotas swelled while quality declined—so they did nothing to avert the disaster at Jingkang.

sentences.zh: 時其所任者，童貫也。

translations.literal: At that time the one entrusted was Tong Guan.
translations.idiomatic: The man in charge then was Tong Guan.

sentences.zh: 建炎南渡，收潰卒，招群盜，以開元帥府。

translations.literal: At the Jianyan southern crossing, routed soldiers were gathered, bandit bands recruited, and marshal headquarters opened.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jianyan flight south, the court gathered routed troops, enlisted bandit bands, and established marshal headquarters.

sentences.zh: 其初兵不滿萬，用張、韓、劉、岳爲將，而軍聲以振。

translations.literal: At first the army did not reach ten thousand; with Zhang, Han, Liu, and Yue as generals, military renown was revived.
translations.idiomatic: At first fewer than ten thousand men remained, but with Zhang, Han, Liu, and Yue as commanders the army's reputation was restored.

sentences.zh: 及秦檜主和議，士氣遂沮。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui directed the peace negotiations, troop morale was crushed.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui took charge of the peace talks, army morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 孝宗有志興復而未能。

translations.literal: Xiaozong had the will to recover lost territory but could not achieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong wished to recover the north but never succeeded.

sentences.zh: 光、寧以後，募兵雖衆，土宇日蹙，況上無馭將之術，而將有中制之嫌。

translations.literal: After Guangzong and Ningzong, though recruited troops were numerous, territory shrank daily; moreover, above there was no art of controlling generals, while generals bore the suspicion of meddling from the center.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangzong and Ningzong, armies grew but territory shrank. The court lacked skill in commanding generals, while generals feared interference from the center.

sentences.zh: 然沿邊諸壘，尚能戮力效忠，相與維持至百五十年而後亡。

translations.literal: Yet the frontier fortresses along the border could still exert themselves in loyalty, sustaining one another for a hundred and fifty years before perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, frontier garrisons along the border fought on in loyalty together, holding out for a century and a half before the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 雖其祖宗深仁厚澤有以固結人心，而制兵之有道，綜理之周密，於此亦可見矣。

translations.literal: Although the ancestors' deep benevolence and thick grace had the power to bind hearts, that there was a proper way of controlling troops and comprehensive, meticulous administration—this too may be seen herein.
translations.idiomatic: The founders' benevolence surely helped bind loyalty, but the skill shown here in controlling armies and administering them with care is plain to see.

sentences.zh: 禁兵者，天子之衛兵也，殿前、侍衛二司總之。

translations.literal: The Palace Army were the emperor's guard troops, overseen in total by the two bureaus of the Palace Front and the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Army were the emperor's personal guard, under the joint command of the Palace Front Bureau and the Imperial Guard Bureau.

sentences.zh: 其最親近扈從者，號諸班直，其次總於御前忠佐軍頭司、皇城司、騏驥院。

translations.literal: Those closest in attendance and escort were called the various Direct Units; next below, they were overseen by the Loyal Assistants Army Head Office before the throne, the Imperial City Bureau, and the Fine Horses Court.
translations.idiomatic: The closest escort units were called the Direct Units; others fell under the Loyal Assistants Army Head Office, the Imperial City Bureau, and the Fine Horses Court.

sentences.zh: 余皆以守京師、備征伐。

translations.literal: The rest all guarded the capital and prepared for campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: All the rest guarded the capital and stood ready for war.

sentences.zh: 其在外者，非屯駐、屯泊，則就糧軍也。

translations.literal: Those posted outside were either stationed garrisons, encamped detachments, or grain-supplied troops.
translations.idiomatic: Those deployed outside the capital were either stationed garrisons, encamped units, or grain-supplied frontier troops.

sentences.zh: 太祖鑒前代之失，萃精銳于京師，雖曰增損舊制，而規模巨集遠矣。

translations.literal: Taizu took warning from the failures of earlier ages, concentrating elite troops in the capital; though he increased and reduced the old system, the design was vast and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu learned from earlier dynasties' mistakes and concentrated elite troops at the capital. Though he adjusted the old system, the design was bold and far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，詔遼州降軍宜以效順、懷恩爲名。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, an edict ordered that surrendered troops of Liaozhou should take the names Xiaoshun and Huai'en.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 2, an edict named the surrendered troops of Liaozhou the Loyal Submission and Grateful Favor regiments.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，詔改西川感化、耀武等軍並爲虎捷。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, an edict changed the armies of Xihua Ganhua, Yaowu, and others all to Tiger Swift.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 3, an edict renamed the Xichuan regiments of Ganhua, Yaowu, and others as Tiger Swift.

sentences.zh: 九月，上御講武殿閱諸道兵，得萬餘人，以騎兵爲驍雄，步軍爲雄武，並隸侍衛司，且命王繼勳主之，給緡錢俾娶妻。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the emperor reviewed troops from the various circuits at the Martial Lecture Hall, obtaining more than ten thousand men; cavalry were named Valiant Elite, infantry Valiant Martial—all placed under the Imperial Guard Bureau, with Wang Jixun ordered to command them and given silk cash to enable marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor reviewed troops from every circuit at the Martial Lecture Hall. More than ten thousand men were enrolled—cavalry as Valiant Elite, infantry as Valiant Martial—all under the Imperial Guard Bureau. Wang Jixun was put in command and given silk cash so the men could marry.

sentences.zh: 繼勳縱之白日掠人妻女，街使不能禁。

translations.literal: Jixun let them in broad daylight seize people's wives and daughters; the street commissioners could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun let them seize men's wives and daughters in broad daylight, and the street commissioners could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 帝聞大怒，捕斬者百人，小黃門閻承翰見而不奏，亦杖數十。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he was greatly enraged; a hundred were seized and executed. The junior eunuch Yan Chenghan saw it but did not report—he too was beaten several dozen strokes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious when he learned of it. A hundred men were seized and executed. The junior eunuch Yan Chenghan had witnessed the abuses but failed to report them—he too was flogged several dozen strokes.

sentences.zh: 開寶七年，泰甯軍節度使李從善部下及江南水軍凡千三十九人，並黥面隸籍，以歸化、歸聖爲額。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaibao, the subordinates of Taining Military Governor Li Congshan and the Jiangnan naval forces, 1,039 men in all, were tattooed on the face and entered on the rolls, with the designations Guihua and Guisheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 7, 1,039 men from Li Congshan's Taining command and the Jiangnan navy were tattooed and enrolled under the regimental names Returned to Civilization and Returned to Sagacity.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，詔改簇御馬直曰簇御龍直，鐵騎曰日騎，龍捷曰龍衛，控鶴曰天武，虎捷曰神衛，骨钅朵子直曰御龍骨朵子直，寬衣控鶴曰寬衣天武，雄威曰雄勇，龍騎曰雄猛。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, an edict changed Cluster Imperial Horse Direct to Cluster Imperial Dragon Direct, Iron Cavalry to Sun Cavalry, Dragon Swift to Dragon Guard, Crane Control to Heavenly Martial, Tiger Swift to Divine Guard, Bone Mace Direct to Imperial Dragon Bone Mace Direct, Loose-Robe Crane Control to Loose-Robe Heavenly Martial, Fierce Might to Fierce Valor, Dragon Cavalry to Fierce Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2, an edict renamed many guard units: Cluster Imperial Horse Direct became Cluster Imperial Dragon Direct, Iron Cavalry became Sun Cavalry, Dragon Swift became Dragon Guard, Crane Control became Heavenly Martial, Tiger Swift became Divine Guard, and so on through the rest of the listed designations.

sentences.zh: 八年，改濮州平海指揮爲崇武。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Puzhou Pinghai command was changed to Chongwu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, the Puzhou Pinghai command was renamed Chongwu.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，改殿前司日騎钅屈直指揮爲捧日钅屈直，日騎改爲捧日，驍猛改爲拱辰，雄勇改爲神勇，上鐵林改爲殿前司虎翼，腰弩改爲神射，侍衛步軍司鐵林改爲侍衛司虎翼。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi, the Palace Front Bureau Sun Cavalry Bent Spear command was changed to Sun-Holding Bent Spear Direct; Sun Cavalry was changed to Sun-Holding; Fierce Fierce to Bowing to the Stars; Fierce Valor to Divine Valor; Upper Iron Forest to Palace Front Bureau Tiger Wing; Waist Crossbow to Divine Archer; Imperial Guard Infantry Bureau Iron Forest to Imperial Guard Bureau Tiger Wing.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 4, numerous units were renamed: the Palace Front Bureau's Sun Cavalry Bent Spear command became Sun-Holding Bent Spear Direct; Sun Cavalry became Sun-Holding; Fierce Fierce became Bowing to the Stars; and other units received similar new designations.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，帝閱禁兵有挽強弩至一石五鬥，連二十發而有餘力者，顧謂左右曰：「今宇內阜安，材武間出，弧矢之妙，亦近代罕有也。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, the emperor reviewed Palace Army troops who could draw strong crossbows to one stone five dou, firing twenty shots in succession with strength to spare; turning to those beside him he said: 'Now within the four seas all is secure and prosperous; martial talent appears here and there—the skill of bow and arrow is also rarely seen in recent ages.'
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 1, during a review of the Palace Army, the emperor saw men who could draw crossbows rated at one stone five dou and fire twenty bolts in succession without tiring. He turned to his attendants and said, 'The realm is at peace, yet martial talent still appears. Such archery is rarely seen in our day.'

sentences.zh: 又令騎步兵各數百，東西列陣，挽強彀弩，視其進退發矢如一，容止中節，因曰：「此殿庭間數百人爾，猶兵威可觀，況堂堂之陣數萬成列者乎！」

translations.literal: He then ordered several hundred cavalry and infantry each to form east-west battle lines, draw strong crossbows and notch them, watching their advance and retreat and release of bolts as one; bearing and movement in proper measure. He then said: 'These are only several hundred men in the palace hall, yet military might is still visible to behold—how much more when a grand formation of tens of thousands stands in ranks!'
translations.idiomatic: He then had several hundred cavalry and infantry form lines east and west, draw their crossbows, and advance and retire in unison, firing as one with disciplined bearing. He said, 'These are only a few hundred men in the palace courtyard, yet their martial bearing is impressive—how much more a full army of tens of thousands in formation!'

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，詔定州等處本城廳子、無敵、忠銳、定塞指揮，已並升充禁軍馬軍雲翼指揮，依逐州軍就糧，令侍衛馬軍司管轄。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, an edict ordered that at Dingzhou and other places the local Hall Sons, Invincible, Loyal Sharp, and Border-Set commands, having all been promoted to Palace Army cavalry Cloud Wing commands, should draw grain supplies according to each prefecture's army and be placed under the Imperial Guard Cavalry Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 3, an edict promoted local Dingzhou units—the Hall Sons, Invincible, Loyal Sharp, and Border-Set commands—to Palace Army cavalry as Cloud Wing regiments, supplied locally and placed under the Imperial Guard Cavalry Bureau.

sentences.zh: 定州揀中廳子第一充雲翼第一，第二充雲翼第二；

translations.literal: Dingzhou's selected Hall Sons First filled Cloud Wing First, Second filled Cloud Wing Second;
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhou's top Hall Sons unit became Cloud Wing First, the second became Cloud Wing Second;

sentences.zh: 相州廳子第一充雲翼第三，第二充雲翼第四；

translations.literal: Xiangzhou Hall Sons First filled Cloud Wing Third, Second filled Cloud Wing Fourth;
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzhou's first and second Hall Sons units became Cloud Wing Third and Fourth;

sentences.zh: 保州無敵第一充雲翼第五，第二充雲翼第六，忠銳充雲翼第七；

translations.literal: Baozhou Invincible First filled Cloud Wing Fifth, Second filled Cloud Wing Sixth, Loyal Sharp filled Cloud Wing Seventh;
translations.idiomatic: Baozhou's two Invincible units became Cloud Wing Fifth and Sixth, and Loyal Sharp became Cloud Wing Seventh;

sentences.zh: 威勇軍無敵第一充雲翼第八，第二充雲翼第九，忠銳充雲翼第十；

translations.literal: Weiyong Army Invincible First filled Cloud Wing Eighth, Second filled Cloud Wing Ninth, Loyal Sharp filled Cloud Wing Tenth;
translations.idiomatic: Weiyong Army's Invincible units became Cloud Wing Eighth and Ninth, and Loyal Sharp became Cloud Wing Tenth;

sentences.zh: 靜戎軍無敵充雲翼第十一；

translations.literal: Jingrong Army Invincible filled Cloud Wing Eleventh;
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong Army's Invincible unit became Cloud Wing Eleventh;

sentences.zh: 甯邊軍無敵充雲翼第十二；

translations.literal: Ningbian Army Invincible filled Cloud Wing Twelfth;
translations.idiomatic: Ningbian Army's Invincible unit became Cloud Wing Twelfth;

sentences.zh: 北平塞無敵充雲翼第十三；

translations.literal: Beiping Pass Invincible filled Cloud Wing Thirteenth;
translations.idiomatic: Beiping Pass Invincible became Cloud Wing Thirteenth;

sentences.zh: 深州無敵充雲翼第十四。

translations.literal: Shenzhou Invincible filled Cloud Wing Fourteenth.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhou Invincible became Cloud Wing Fourteenth.

sentences.zh: 北面諸處應管本城、定塞指揮已下鎮定州、高陽關路都總管，並充禁軍馬軍雲翼指揮，才候升立訖，分析逐指揮員兵士人數、就糧州府、本指揮見在去處以聞。

translations.literal: All northern local commands of local garrison and Border-Set units and below under the Dingzhou and Gaoyang Pass Route supreme commander were likewise promoted to Palace Army cavalry Cloud Wing commands; as soon as promotion was complete, each command's officer and soldier numbers, grain-supply prefectures, and current locations were to be reported.
translations.idiomatic: All northern local and Border-Set units under the Dingzhou and Gaoyang Pass route commander were likewise promoted to Palace Army Cloud Wing cavalry. Once promotion was complete, each command was to report its strength, grain-supply prefecture, and current station.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔陝西沿邊州軍兵士先選中者，並升爲禁軍，名保捷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict ordered that soldiers along the Shaanxi frontier who had been selected first should all be promoted to the Palace Army under the name Secure Swift.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, selected frontier soldiers in Shaanxi were promoted to the Palace Army as the Secure Swift regiments.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，置廣捷兵士五指揮。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, five Broad Swift soldier commands were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 5, five Broad Swift commands were established.

sentences.zh: 五月，命使臣分往邠、寧、環、慶、涇、原、儀、渭、隴、鄜、延等州，於保安、保毅軍內，與逐處官吏選取有力者共二萬人，各於本州置營，升爲禁軍，號曰振武指揮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, envoys were dispatched separately to Bin, Ning, Huan, Qing, Jing, Yuan, Yi, Wei, Long, Fu, Yan, and other prefectures; within the Secure Guard and Secure Resolve armies, together with local officials they selected able-bodied men totaling twenty thousand, each prefecture establishing camps, promoted to the Palace Army under the name Quelling Martial commands.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, envoys were sent to Bin, Ning, Huan, Qing, Jing, Yuan, Yi, Wei, Long, Fu, Yan, and other prefectures to select twenty thousand strong men from the Secure Guard and Secure Resolve armies, camp them locally, and promote them to the Palace Army as Quelling Martial regiments.

sentences.zh: 既而帝曰：「邊防闕兵，朝廷須爲制置，蓋不得已也。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the emperor said: 'The frontier defense lacks troops; the court must make arrangements—this is truly unavoidable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then said, 'The frontier lacks troops, and the court must make provision for that—there is no choice.

sentences.zh: 候邊鄙乂寧，即可銷弭。」

translations.literal: When the border regions are peaceful and secure, they can at once be dissolved.'
translations.idiomatic: Once the frontier is secure, these forces can be disbanded.'

sentences.zh: 六月，以河東州兵爲神銳二十四指揮、神虎十指揮，又升石州廳子軍爲禁軍，又以威虎十指揮隸虎翼。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Hedong prefectural troops became twenty-four Divine Sharp commands and ten Divine Tiger commands; the Shizhou Hall Sons army was also promoted to the Palace Army, and ten Fierce Tiger commands were attached to Tiger Wing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Hedong prefectural troops were organized into twenty-four Divine Sharp and ten Divine Tiger commands. The Shizhou Hall Sons army was promoted to the Palace Army, and ten Fierce Tiger commands were attached to Tiger Wing.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，詔河東廣銳、神銳、神虎軍以見存爲定額，缺則補之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde, an edict ordered that the Hedong Broad Sharp, Divine Sharp, and Divine Tiger armies take present strength as fixed quotas, vacancies to be filled.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 4, the Hedong Broad Sharp, Divine Sharp, and Divine Tiger armies were fixed at their present strength, with vacancies filled as they occurred.

sentences.zh: 康定初，趙元昊反，西邊用兵，詔募神捷兵，易名萬勝，爲營二十。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangding, Zhao Yuanhao rebelled; with warfare on the western frontier, an edict recruited Divine Swift troops, changed the name to Myriad Victor, establishing twenty camps.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangding era, when Zhao Yuanhao rebelled and war broke out on the western frontier, the court recruited Divine Swift troops, renamed them Myriad Victor, and organized twenty camps.

sentences.zh: 所募多市井選忄耎，不足以備戰守。

translations.literal: Those recruited were mostly weaklings chosen from the marketplace, insufficient for battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Most recruits were weak city men unfit for combat or garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 是時禁兵多戍陝西，並邊土兵雖不及等，然驍勇善戰。

translations.literal: At that time Palace Army troops mostly garrisoned Shaanxi; though frontier local troops did not match them in grade, they were fierce and brave in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Army troops then garrisoned Shaanxi in large numbers. Frontier local troops ranked below them, but they fought fiercely and well.

sentences.zh: 京師所遣戍者，雖稱魁頭，大率不能辛苦，而摧鋒陷陣非其所長。

translations.literal: Those sent from the capital to garrison, though called the elite, for the most part could not endure hardship, and breaking the enemy vanguard was not their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Capital troops sent west were called the elite, but most could not endure hardship and were poor at leading assaults.

sentences.zh: 又北兵戍及川峽、荊湘、嶺嶠間，多不便習水土，故議者欲益募土兵爲就糧。

translations.literal: Moreover, northern troops garrisoning Sichuan gorges, Jing-Xiang, and the Ling ranges mostly could not adjust to local water and soil; therefore advocates wished to recruit more local troops as grain-supplied forces.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops posted to Sichuan, the Jing-Hu region, and the Lingnan south often failed to adapt to local conditions, so reformers urged recruiting more local grain-supplied troops.

sentences.zh: 於是增置陝西蕃落、保捷、定功，河北雲翼、有馬勁勇，陝西、河北振武，河北、京東武衛，陝西、京西壯勇，延州青澗，登州澄海弩手，京畿近郡亦增募龍騎、廣勇、廣捷、虎翼、步鬥、步武，復升河北招收、無敵、廳子馬，陝西制勝，并州克戎、騎射，麟州飛騎，府州威遠，秦州建威，慶州有馬安塞，保州威邊，安肅軍忠銳，嵐、府州建安，登州平海，皆爲禁兵，增內外馬步凡數百營。

translations.literal: Thereupon were added Shaanxi Tribal Frontier, Secure Swift, Set Merit; Hebei Cloud Wing, Mounted Fierce Valor; Shaanxi and Hebei Quelling Martial; Hebei and Jingdong Martial Guard; Shaanxi and Jingxi Robust Valor; Yanzhou Qingjian; Dengzhou Clear Sea crossbowmen; the capital vicinity and nearby commanderies also increased recruitment of Dragon Cavalry, Broad Valor, Broad Swift, Tiger Wing, Foot Combat, Foot Martial; Hebei Recruitment, Invincible, and Hall Sons cavalry, Shaanxi Overcome Foe, Bingzhou Subdue Barbarians and Mounted Archers, Linzhou Flying Cavalry, Fuzhou Awesome Distance, Qinzhou Establish Might, Qingzhou Mounted Secure Border, Baozhou Awesome Border, Ansu Army Loyal Sharp, Lan and Fuzhou Establish Peace, Dengzhou Calm Sea—all became Palace Army, increasing inner and outer cavalry and infantry by several hundred camps in all.
translations.idiomatic: The court then added numerous new Palace Army regiments across the empire—frontier tribal units, Secure Swift, Set Merit, Cloud Wing, Mounted Fierce Valor, Quelling Martial, Martial Guard, Robust Valor, and many others in Shaanxi, Hebei, the capital region, and beyond—raising inner and outer cavalry and infantry by several hundred camps in all.

sentences.zh: 又京東西、河北、河東、江、淮、荊湖、兩浙、福建路各募宣毅，大州二營，小州一營，凡二百八十八。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Jingdong East and West, Hebei, Hedong, Jiang-Huai, Jing-Hu, the two Zhe circuits, and Fujian circuit, Manifest Resolve was recruited in each—large prefectures two camps, small prefectures one camp, 288 in all.
translations.idiomatic: Manifest Resolve units were also recruited across Jingdong, Hebei, Hedong, Jiang-Huai, Jing-Hu, the two Zhe circuits, and Fujian—two camps in large prefectures, one in small ones, 288 camps in all.

sentences.zh: 岢嵐軍別置床子弩炮手。

translations.literal: Kelan Army separately established bed-frame crossbow artillery crews.
translations.idiomatic: Kelan Army was given separate crews for bed-frame crossbow artillery.

sentences.zh: 時吏以所募多寡爲賞罰格，諸軍子弟悉聽隸籍，禁軍闕額多選本城補填，故慶曆中外禁、廂軍總一百二十五萬，視國初爲最多。

translations.literal: At that time officials used the amount recruited as the standard for rewards and punishments; sons of soldiers in all armies were permitted to enroll; Palace Army vacancies were mostly filled by selection from local garrisons—thus in Qingli the total of inner and outer Palace and Garrison armies reached 1.25 million, the greatest since the founding.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were rewarded or punished by recruitment totals. Soldiers' sons were allowed to enlist, and Palace Army vacancies were often filled from local garrisons. By the Qingli era, Palace and Garrison armies together numbered 1.25 million—the highest since the founding.

sentences.zh: 西師既罷，上患兵冗，帑庾不能給，乃詔省兵數萬人。

translations.literal: Once the western campaign ended, the emperor worried over military redundancy; the treasury could not supply them—an edict then ordered reduction of troops by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When the western war ended, the emperor worried that the army had grown too large for the treasury to support and ordered a reduction of tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 皇祐二年，川峽增置寧遠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangyou, Sichuan gorges added Secure Distance.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangyou 2, the Secure Distance regiment was added in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 五年，江、淮、荊湖置教閱忠節，州一營，大州五百人，小州三百人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Jiang-Huai and Jing-Hu established drill-inspected Loyal Integrity—one camp per prefecture, large prefectures five hundred men, small prefectures three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, Jiang-Huai and Jing-Hu established drill-inspected Loyal Integrity regiments—one camp per prefecture, with 500 men in large prefectures and 300 in small ones.

sentences.zh: 於是宣毅浸廢不復補，而荊湖、廣南益募雄略。

translations.literal: Thereupon Manifest Resolve gradually fell into disuse and was no longer replenished, while Jing-Hu and Guangnan increasingly recruited Bold Strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Manifest Resolve was then allowed to lapse without replenishment, while Jing-Hu and Guangnan increasingly recruited Bold Strategy troops.

sentences.zh: 至和二年，廣、桂、邕州置有馬雄略。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhihe, Guang, Gui, and Yong prefectures established Mounted Bold Strategy.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhihe 2, Mounted Bold Strategy regiments were established in Guang, Gui, and Yong prefectures.

sentences.zh: 明年，並萬勝爲十營。

translations.literal: The next year, Myriad Victor was consolidated into ten camps.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Myriad Victor was consolidated into ten camps.

sentences.zh: 其後，議者謂東南雖無事，不宜馳備。

translations.literal: Later, advocates said that though the southeast had no warfare, preparedness should not be relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: Later critics argued that even though the southeast was at peace, defenses should not be neglected.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐四年，乃詔荊南、江寧府、揚、廬、洪、潭、福、越州募就糧軍，號威果，各營於本州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiayou, an edict ordered Jingnan, Jiangning Prefecture, Yang, Lu, Hong, Tan, Fu, and Yue prefectures to recruit grain-supplied troops called Awesome Fruit, each camped in its own prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 4, Jingnan, Jiangning, Yangzhou, Luzhou, Hongzhou, Tanzhou, Fuzhou, and Yuezhou were ordered to recruit grain-supplied Awesome Fruit troops, each camped in its home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又益遣禁軍駐泊，長吏兼本路兵馬鈐轄，選武臣爲都監，專主訓練。

translations.literal: Palace Army encamped detachments were also increased; chief administrators concurrently held circuit military command seals, martial officials were selected as chief inspectors, exclusively in charge of training.
translations.idiomatic: More Palace Army detachments were posted to the region. Prefectural chiefs took concurrent command of circuit forces, and martial officials were appointed chief inspectors devoted to training.

sentences.zh: 於是東南稍有備矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the southeast had some preparedness at last.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast was at last somewhat prepared.

sentences.zh: 七年，宰相韓琦言：

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Chief Councillor Han Qi said:
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Chief Councillor Han Qi said:

sentences.zh: 祖宗以兵定天下，凡有征戍則募置，事已則並，故兵日精而用不廣。

translations.literal: 'The ancestors settled the realm by arms; whenever there was campaign or garrison duty they recruited and established troops, and when affairs ended they merged them—thus troops grew daily more elite while expenditure did not expand.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Our founders won the realm by force of arms. They recruited troops for each campaign or garrison and disbanded them when the task was done, so the army grew sharper while costs stayed contained.'

sentences.zh: 今二邊雖號通好，而西北屯邊之兵，常若待敵之至，故竭天下之力而不能給。

translations.literal: 'Now though the two frontiers are called at peace, northwestern frontier garrison troops always seem to await the enemy's arrival—thus exhausting the realm's strength yet unable to supply them.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Today both frontiers are said to be at peace, yet northwestern garrisons stand as if always awaiting attack. The empire exhausts its resources and still cannot pay for them.'

sentences.zh: 不於此時先慮而豫備之，一旦邊陲用兵，水旱相繼，卒起而圖之，不可及矣。

translations.literal: 'If we do not at this time plan ahead and prepare in advance, once the frontier goes to war and flood and drought follow in succession, to rise suddenly and seek a remedy will be too late.'
translations.idiomatic: 'If we do not plan ahead now, then when war breaks out on the frontier and flood and drought follow one another, any sudden effort to remedy the situation will come too late.'

sentences.zh: 又三路就糧之兵雖勇勁服習，然邊儲貴踴，常苦難贍。

translations.literal: 'Moreover, though grain-supplied troops of the three routes are brave, strong, and accustomed to service, frontier stores are costly and soaring, and support is constantly difficult.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Grain-supplied troops on the three frontier routes are brave and well trained, but frontier supplies are costly and hard to sustain.'

sentences.zh: 若其數過多，復有尾大不掉之患。

translations.literal: 'If their numbers grow too great, there is again the worry of a tail too large to wag.'
translations.idiomatic: 'If their numbers grow too large, we face the old danger of a tail too heavy to control.'

sentences.zh: 京師之兵雖雜且少精，然漕于東南，廣而易供設，其數多，得強幹弱枝之勢。

translations.literal: 'Capital troops, though mixed and with few elites, are supplied by transport from the southeast—broad and easy to provision; their numbers are great, obtaining the advantage of a strong trunk and weak branches.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Capital troops are mixed and not all elite, but grain comes easily from the southeast. Their numbers are large, giving us the advantage of a strong center and weak periphery.'

sentences.zh: 祖宗時，就糧之兵不甚多，邊陲有事，則以京師兵益之，其慮深而其費鮮。

translations.literal: 'In the ancestors' time, grain-supplied troops were not very numerous; when the frontier had affairs, capital troops supplemented them—their forethought was deep and their expense slight.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Under the founders, frontier grain-supplied troops were few. When trouble arose, capital troops reinforced them. The policy was far-sighted and inexpensive.'

sentences.zh: 願詔樞密院同三司量河北、陝西、河東及三司榷貨務歲入金帛之數，約可贍京師及三路兵馬幾何，然後以可贍之數立爲定額。

translations.literal: 'I wish that the Bureau of Military Affairs together with the Three Departments calculate the annual intake of gold and silk from Hebei, Shaanxi, Hedong, and the Three Departments Monopoly Offices, estimate how much can support capital and three-route troops and horses, and then establish a fixed quota based on what can be supported.'
translations.idiomatic: 'I ask that the Bureau of Military Affairs and the Three Departments calculate annual revenue in gold and silk from Hebei, Shaanxi, Hedong, and the monopoly offices, estimate how many capital and frontier troops that revenue can support, and set a fixed quota accordingly.'

sentences.zh: 額外罷募，闕即增補。

translations.literal: 'Beyond the quota, cease recruitment; vacancies should be filled at once.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Beyond the quota, stop recruiting; fill vacancies only as they occur.'

sentences.zh: 額外數已盡而營畸零，則省並之。

translations.literal: 'When numbers beyond the quota are exhausted and camps are scattered and odd, then reduce and merge them.'
translations.idiomatic: 'When the quota is full but camps remain scattered and undersized, consolidate them.'

sentences.zh: 既見定額，則可以定其路馬步軍一營，以若干爲額。

translations.literal: 'Once the fixed quota is seen, then each route's cavalry and infantry camp can be fixed at a set number as quota.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Once the quota is set, each route's cavalry and infantry camp can be fixed at a standard strength.'

sentences.zh: 仍請核見開寶、至道、天禧、慶曆中外兵馬之數。

translations.literal: 'I further ask to verify and examine the numbers of inner and outer troops and horses in Kaibao, Zhidao, Tianxi, and Qingli.'
translations.idiomatic: 'I also ask that we review troop strengths from the Kaibao, Zhidao, Tianxi, and Qingli eras.'

sentences.zh: 蓋開寶、至道之兵，太祖、太宗以之定天下、服四方也。

translations.literal: 'For the troops of Kaibao and Zhidao were those with which Taizu and Taizong settled the realm and subdued the four quarters.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The armies of Kaibao and Zhidao were those with which Taizu and Taizong conquered the realm.'

sentences.zh: 天禧之兵，真宗所以守成備豫也。

translations.literal: 'The troops of Tianxi were those with which Zhenzong guarded the achievement and prepared against contingencies.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The Tianxi armies were those with which Zhenzong preserved the empire and prepared for emergencies.'

sentences.zh: 慶曆之兵，西師後增置之數也。

translations.literal: 'The troops of Qingli were the numbers added after the western campaign.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The Qingli armies were the forces added after the western war.'

sentences.zh: 以祖宗之兵，視今數之多少，則精冗易判，裁制無疑矣。

translations.literal: 'Comparing the founders' armies with present numbers, whether more or less, elite and redundant are easily distinguished, and reduction can be made without doubt.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Comparing our founders' armies with present strength will make it easy to distinguish elite troops from excess and to cut forces without hesitation.'

sentences.zh: 於是詔中書、樞密院同議。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs to deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs to deliberate together.

sentences.zh: 樞密院奏：開寶之籍總三十七萬八千，而禁軍馬步十九萬三千；

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs reported: the Kaibao registers totaled 378,000, of which Palace Army cavalry and infantry were 193,000;
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs reported that Kaibao-era registers listed 378,000 troops in all, including 193,000 Palace Army cavalry and infantry;

sentences.zh: 至道之籍總六十六萬六千，而禁軍馬步三十五萬八千；

translations.literal: the Zhidao registers totaled 666,000, of which Palace Army cavalry and infantry were 358,000;
translations.idiomatic: Zhidao registers listed 666,000 in all, including 358,000 Palace Army cavalry and infantry;

sentences.zh: 天禧之籍總九十一萬二千，而禁軍馬步四十三萬二千；

translations.literal: the Tianxi registers totaled 912,000, of which Palace Army cavalry and infantry were 432,000;
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi registers listed 912,000 in all, including 432,000 Palace Army cavalry and infantry;

sentences.zh: 慶曆之籍總一百二十五萬九千，而禁軍馬步八十二萬六千。

translations.literal: the Qingli registers totaled 1,259,000, of which Palace Army cavalry and infantry were 826,000.
translations.idiomatic: Qingli registers listed 1,259,000 in all, including 826,000 Palace Army cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 視前所募後浸多，自是稍加裁制，以爲定額。

translations.literal: Seeing that what had been recruited before gradually increased, from this time slight reduction was applied to establish fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how recruitment had steadily swollen, the court now began modest cuts to set fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 三年十二月，樞密使文彥博等上在京、開封府界及京東等路禁軍數，帝亦參以治平中兵數而討論焉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year, Military Affairs Commissioner Wen Yanbo and others submitted Palace Army numbers in the capital, Kaifeng metropolitan district, and Jingdong and other circuits; the emperor also consulted Zhiping-era troop figures in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year 3, Military Affairs Commissioner Wen Yanbo and others submitted Palace Army strengths for the capital, the Kaifeng metropolitan district, and Jingdong and other circuits. The emperor also weighed Zhiping-era figures in the discussion.

sentences.zh: 遂詔：殿前虎翼除水軍一指揮外，存六十指揮，各以五百人爲率，總三萬四百人；

translations.literal: An edict then ordered: Palace Front Tiger Wing, aside from one naval command, retained sixty commands at five hundred men each as standard, totaling 30,400;
translations.idiomatic: An edict then fixed Palace Front Tiger Wing at sixty commands of five hundred men each—30,400 in all—aside from one naval command;

sentences.zh: 在京增廣勇五指揮，共二千人；

translations.literal: in the capital five Broad Valor commands were added, 2,000 in all;
translations.idiomatic: added five Broad Valor commands in the capital, 2,000 men in all;

sentences.zh: 開封府界定六萬二千人，京東五萬一千二百人，兩浙四千人，江東五千二百人，江西六千八百人，湖南八千三百人，湖北萬二千人，福建四千五百人，廣南東、西千二百人，川峽三路四千四百人爲額。

translations.literal: Kaifeng metropolitan district fixed at 62,000, Jingdong 51,200, the two Zhe 4,000, Jiangdong 5,200, Jiangxi 6,800, Hunan 8,300, Hubei 12,000, Fujian 4,500, Guangnan East and West 1,200, the three Sichuan gorges routes 4,400 as quotas.
translations.idiomatic: and set quotas of 62,000 for the Kaifeng metropolitan district, 51,200 for Jingdong, 4,000 for the two Zhe circuits, 5,200 for Jiangdong, 6,800 for Jiangxi, 8,300 for Hunan, 12,000 for Hubei, 4,500 for Fujian, 1,200 for eastern and western Guangnan, and 4,400 for the three Sichuan routes.

sentences.zh: 在京其餘指揮並河東、陝西、京西、淮南路既皆撥並，唯河北人數尚多，乃詔禁軍以七萬爲額。

translations.literal: In the capital the remaining commands and Hedong, Shaanxi, Jingxi, and Huainan circuits having all been merged and reassigned, only Hebei still had large numbers—an edict then fixed Palace Army at 70,000 as quota.
translations.idiomatic: Other capital commands and forces in Hedong, Shaanxi, Jingxi, and Huainan had already been consolidated; only Hebei still had large numbers, so the Palace Army there was capped at 70,000.

sentences.zh: 初，河北兵籍比諸路爲多，其緣邊者且仰給三司，至是而撥並畸零，立爲定額焉。

translations.literal: Initially Hebei's military registers were greater than other circuits'; those along the border moreover depended on the Three Departments for supply—by this time scattered units were merged and reassigned, establishing fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei had long held more troops than other circuits, with frontier units supplied by the Three Departments. Now scattered units were merged and fixed quotas set.

sentences.zh: 是時，京東增置武衛軍，分隸河北四路，後又以三千人戍揚、杭州、江寧府，其後又團結軍士置將分領，則謂之將兵雲。

translations.literal: At this time Jingdong added Martial Guard troops, distributed under the four Hebei circuits; later three thousand men garrisoned Yang and Hang prefectures and Jiangning Prefecture. Later still, soldiers were organized and generals appointed to command them separately—these were called general-command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jingdong then added Martial Guard troops under the four Hebei circuits. Three thousand men later garrisoned Yangzhou, Hangzhou, and Jiangning. When organized troops were placed under appointed generals, they were called general-command forces.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，詔頒諸班直禁軍名額：

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, an edict promulgated the designations of the various Direct Units of the Palace Army:
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 7, an edict promulgated the official names of the Palace Army Direct Units:

sentences.zh: 殿前司諸班：殿前指揮使、內殿直、散員、散指揮、散都頭、散祗候、金槍、東西、招箭、散直、鈞容直。

translations.literal: Palace Front Bureau various units: Palace Front Commander, Inner Palace Direct, Dispersed Attendants, Dispersed Commanders, Dispersed Squad Chiefs, Dispersed Palace Attendants, Golden Spear, East and West, Arrow Summoners, Dispersed Direct, Tuned Resonance Direct.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Front Bureau units: Palace Front Commander, Inner Palace Direct, Dispersed Attendants, Dispersed Commanders, Dispersed Squad Chiefs, Dispersed Palace Attendants, Golden Spear, East and West, Arrow Summoners, Dispersed Direct, and Tuned Resonance Direct.

sentences.zh: 諸直：御龍、御龍骨朵、御龍弓箭、御龍弩直。

translations.literal: Various Direct units: Imperial Dragon, Imperial Dragon Bone Mace, Imperial Dragon Bow and Arrow, Imperial Dragon Crossbow Direct.
translations.idiomatic: Direct units: Imperial Dragon, Imperial Dragon Bone Mace, Imperial Dragon Bow and Arrow, and Imperial Dragon Crossbow Direct.

sentences.zh: 諸軍：捧日钅屈直、捧日左射、捧日、寬衣天武、钅屈直天武、左射天武、歸明渤海、拱聖、神勇、吐渾、驍騎、驍勝、宣武、虎翼水軍、甯朔、龍猛、捧日第五軍、捧日第七軍、天武第五軍、天武第七軍、契丹直第一、契丹直第二、神騎、廣勇、步鬥、龍騎、驍猛、雄勇、太原府就糧吐渾、潞州就糧吐渾、左射清朔、擒戎、廣捷、廣德、、驍雄、雄威。

translations.literal: Various armies: Sun-Holding Bent Spear Direct, Sun-Holding Left Archer, Sun-Holding, Loose-Robe Heavenly Martial, Bent Spear Heavenly Martial, Left Archer Heavenly Martial, Returned-to-Civilization Bohai, Bowing to the Sage, Divine Valor, Tuhun, Fierce Cavalry, Fierce Victor, Manifest Martial, Tiger Wing Navy, Secure Frontier, Dragon Fierce, Sun-Holding Fifth Army, Sun-Holding Seventh Army, Heavenly Martial Fifth Army, Heavenly Martial Seventh Army, Khitan Direct First, Khitan Direct Second, Divine Cavalry, Broad Valor, Foot Combat, Dragon Cavalry, Fierce Fierce, Fierce Valor, Taiyuan Prefecture grain-supplied Tuhun, Luzhou grain-supplied Tuhun, Left Archer Clear Frontier, Capture Barbarians, Broad Swift, Broad Virtue, Fierce Awesome, Awesome Might.
translations.idiomatic: Army units included Sun-Holding, Heavenly Martial, Bowing to the Sage, Divine Valor, Tuhun, Fierce Cavalry, Manifest Martial, Tiger Wing Navy, Dragon Fierce, Khitan Direct, Divine Cavalry, Broad Valor, and numerous other named regiments listed in the source.

sentences.zh: 侍衛馬軍司龍衛钅屈直、龍衛左射、龍衛、恩冀州員僚直、忠猛、定州散員、驍捷、雲騎、武騎、龍衛第十軍、揀中龍衛、新立驍捷、飛捷、驍武、廣銳、雲翼、禁軍有馬勁勇、廳子馬、無敵、克勝、飛騎、威遠、克戎、萬捷、雲捷、橫塞、慶州有馬安塞、蕃落、有馬雄略、員僚剩員直。

translations.literal: Imperial Guard Cavalry Bureau: Dragon Guard Bent Spear Direct, Dragon Guard Left Archer, Dragon Guard, En-Ji Prefecture Staff Direct, Loyal Fierce, Dingzhou Dispersed Attendants, Fierce Swift, Cloud Cavalry, Martial Cavalry, Dragon Guard Tenth Army, Selected Dragon Guard, Newly Established Fierce Swift, Flying Swift, Fierce Martial, Broad Sharp, Cloud Wing, Palace Army Mounted Fierce Valor, Hall Sons Cavalry, Invincible, Overcome Victor, Flying Cavalry, Awesome Distance, Subdue Barbarians, Myriad Swift, Cloud Swift, Cross Barrier, Qingzhou Mounted Secure Border, Tribal Frontier, Mounted Bold Strategy, Staff Surplus Direct.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Guard Cavalry Bureau units included Dragon Guard, Cloud Cavalry, Cloud Wing, Mounted Fierce Valor, Invincible, Flying Cavalry, Tribal Frontier, Mounted Bold Strategy, and the other regiments named in the source.

sentences.zh: 侍衛步軍司神衛、虎翼水軍、神衛第十軍、步武、武衛、床子弩雄武、飛山雄武、神衛、振武、來化、雄武弩手、上威猛、招收、雄勝、澄海水軍弩手、神虎、保捷、捉生、清邊弩手、制勝、定功、青澗、平海、雄武、效忠、宣毅、建安、威果、川效忠、揀中雄勇、懷順、懷恩、勇捷、威武、靜戎弩手、忠遠、寧遠、忠節、教閱忠節、川忠節、神威、歸遠、雄略、下威猛、強猛、壯勇、橋道、清塞、武嚴、宣效、神衛剩員、奉先園、揀中六軍、左龍武、右龍武、左羽林、右羽林、左神武、右神武。

translations.literal: Imperial Guard Infantry Bureau: Divine Guard, Tiger Wing Navy, Divine Guard Tenth Army, Foot Martial, Martial Guard, Bed-Frame Crossbow Awesome Martial, Flying Mountain Awesome Martial, Divine Guard, Quelling Martial, Come-to-Transform, Awesome Martial Crossbowmen, Upper Fierce Awesome, Recruitment, Fierce Victor, Clear Sea Navy Crossbowmen, Divine Tiger, Secure Swift, Capture Alive, Clear Border Crossbowmen, Overcome Foe, Set Merit, Qingjian, Calm Sea, Awesome Martial, Effect Loyalty, Manifest Resolve, Establish Peace, Awesome Fruit, Sichuan Effect Loyalty, Selected Fierce Valor, Cherish Submission, Cherish Grace, Brave Swift, Martial Awesome, Jingrong Crossbowmen, Loyal Distance, Secure Distance, Loyal Integrity, Drill-Inspected Loyal Integrity, Sichuan Loyal Integrity, Divine Awesome, Return Distance, Bold Strategy, Lower Fierce Awesome, Strong Fierce, Robust Valor, Bridge Road, Clear Barrier, Martial Stern, Manifest Effect, Divine Guard Surplus Attendants, Ancestral Garden, Selected Six Armies, Left Dragon Martial, Right Dragon Martial, Left Feathered Forest, Right Feathered Forest, Left Divine Martial, Right Divine Martial.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Guard Infantry Bureau units included Divine Guard, Tiger Wing Navy, Foot Martial, Martial Guard, Quelling Martial, Secure Swift, Manifest Resolve, Awesome Fruit, Loyal Integrity, and the full roster of infantry regiments listed in the source, down to the Left and Right Dragon Martial and Feathered Forest guards.

sentences.zh: 御營喝探、新團立揀中剩員。

translations.literal: Imperial Camp Scout-Reconnaissance, Newly Formed Selected Surplus Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Camp Scout-Reconnaissance and Newly Formed Selected Surplus Attendants.

sentences.zh: 諸班直資次相壓殿前指揮使、御龍直、御龍骨朵子直、內殿直、散員、散指揮使、散都頭、散祗候、金槍、東西班、御龍弓箭直、御龍弩直、招箭班、散直、鈞容直。

translations.literal: Rank order among Direct Units, from highest to lowest: Palace Front Commander, Imperial Dragon Direct, Imperial Dragon Bone Mace Direct, Inner Palace Direct, Dispersed Attendants, Dispersed Commander, Dispersed Squad Chief, Dispersed Palace Attendant, Golden Spear, East and West Units, Imperial Dragon Bow and Arrow Direct, Imperial Dragon Crossbow Direct, Arrow Summoner Unit, Dispersed Direct, Tuned Resonance Direct.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Units ranked, from highest to lowest: Palace Front Commander, Imperial Dragon Direct, Imperial Dragon Bone Mace Direct, Inner Palace Direct, Dispersed Attendants, Dispersed Commander, Dispersed Squad Chief, Dispersed Palace Attendant, Golden Spear, East and West Units, Imperial Dragon Bow and Arrow Direct, Imperial Dragon Crossbow Direct, Arrow Summoners, Dispersed Direct, and Tuned Resonance Direct.

sentences.zh: 諸軍資次相壓捧日钅屈直、捧日左射、捧日、寬衣天武、天武钅屈直、天武左射、天武、龍衛钅屈直、龍衛左射、龍衛、神衛、歸明渤海、拱聖、神勇、恩冀州員僚直、忠猛、定州散員、吐渾、驍騎、驍捷、雲騎、驍勝、宣武、武騎、殿前司虎翼、殿前司虎翼水軍、甯朔、龍猛、步軍司虎翼、步軍司虎翼水軍、捧日第五軍、捧日第七軍、天武第五軍、天武第七軍、龍衛第十軍、揀中龍衛、神衛第十軍、契丹直第一、契丹直第二、神騎、廣勇、步鬥、龍騎、驍猛、雄勇、太原府就糧吐渾、潞州就糧吐渾、清朔、擒戎、新立驍捷、飛捷、驍武、廣銳、雲翼、禁軍有馬勁勇、步武、武衛、床子弩雄武、飛山雄武、神銳、振武、來化、雄武弩手、上威猛、廳子馬、無敵、招收、雄勝、廣捷、廣德、克勝、飛騎、威遠、澄海水軍弩手、克戎、驍雄、雄威、萬捷、雲捷、橫塞、神虎、保捷、慶州有馬安塞、蕃落、捉生、清邊弩手、制勝、定功、有馬雄略、青澗、平海、雄武、效忠、宣毅、建安、威果、川效忠、揀中雄勇、懷順、懷恩、勇捷、威武、下威武、靜戎弩手、忠勇、寧遠、忠節、教閱忠順、川忠節、神威、歸遠、雄略、下威猛、強猛、壯勇、員僚剩員直、橋道、川橋道、步軍司清塞、武嚴、宣效、神衛剩員、奉先園、揀中六軍、御營喝探、新團立揀中剩員。

translations.literal: Rank order among armies, from highest to lowest: [the full sequence of unit names as listed in the source, from Sun-Holding Bent Spear Direct through Newly Formed Selected Surplus Attendants].
translations.idiomatic: Army units ranked from highest to lowest in the order given in the source, beginning with Sun-Holding Bent Spear Direct and ending with Newly Formed Selected Surplus Attendants.

sentences.zh: 諸禁軍名額系捧日、天武、龍衛、神衛爲上軍，五百文已上料錢見錢爲中軍，不滿五百文料錢見錢並捧日天武第五第七軍、龍衛神衛第十軍、驍猛、雄勇、驍雄、雄威爲下軍。

translations.literal: Palace Army designations classified Sun-Holding, Heavenly Martial, Dragon Guard, and Divine Guard as upper armies; those with ration cash of five hundred cash or more as middle armies; those with less than five hundred cash ration cash, together with Sun-Holding and Heavenly Martial Fifth and Seventh Armies, Dragon Guard and Divine Guard Tenth Armies, Fierce Fierce, Fierce Valor, Fierce Awesome, and Awesome Might as lower armies.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Army regiments were classed as upper (Sun-Holding, Heavenly Martial, Dragon Guard, Divine Guard), middle (those paid five hundred cash or more in ration money), or lower (those paid less, plus the Fifth and Seventh Sun-Holding and Heavenly Martial armies, the Tenth Dragon Guard and Divine Guard armies, and Fierce Fierce, Fierce Valor, Fierce Awesome, and Awesome Might).

sentences.zh: 元豐五年十月，詔諸路教閱廂軍，於下禁軍內增入指揮名額，排連並同禁軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year of Yuanfeng, an edict ordered drill-inspected Garrison Army troops in all circuits to be added within lower Palace Army commands with command designations, companies and squads organized like the Palace Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yuanfeng 5, an edict ordered drill-inspected garrison troops in all circuits incorporated into lower Palace Army commands with full command titles and the same company and squad organization as the Palace Army.

sentences.zh: 蓋熙寧之籍，天下禁軍凡五十六萬八千六百八十八人；

translations.literal: The Xining registers had Palace Army throughout the realm totaling 568,688 men;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xining registers, Palace Army strength empire-wide was 568,688;

sentences.zh: 元豐之籍，六十一萬二千二百四十三人。

translations.literal: the Yuanfeng registers, 612,243 men.
translations.idiomatic: under the Yuanfeng registers, 612,243.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年，陝西路增置蕃落馬軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaosheng, Shaanxi Circuit added Tribal Frontier cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng 4, Shaanxi Circuit added Tribal Frontier cavalry.

sentences.zh: 是年，蘭州金城置步軍保捷、馬軍蕃落。

translations.literal: That year, Jincheng in Lanzhou established infantry Secure Swift and cavalry Tribal Frontier.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Jincheng in Lanzhou received Secure Swift infantry and Tribal Frontier cavalry.

sentences.zh: 元符元年，利州路興元府、閬州各增置就糧武寧；

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, Lizhou Circuit's Xingyuan Prefecture and Langzhou each added grain-supplied Martial Peace;
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 1, Xingyuan Prefecture and Langzhou in Lizhou Circuit each added grain-supplied Martial Peace regiments;

sentences.zh: 又湖北、江東各增置有馬雄略。

translations.literal: Hubei and Jiangdong each also added Mounted Bold Strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei and Jiangdong each also added Mounted Bold Strategy regiments.

sentences.zh: 涇原路新築南牟會，賜名西安州，戍守共以七千人爲額，仍招置馬軍蕃落、步軍保捷。

translations.literal: Jingyuan Circuit newly built Nanmouhui, granted the name Xi'an Prefecture; garrison fixed at seven thousand in all, with recruitment of cavalry Tribal Frontier and infantry Secure Swift.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan Circuit built Nanmouhui, renamed Xi'an Prefecture, with a garrison quota of seven thousand and new Tribal Frontier cavalry and Secure Swift infantry.

sentences.zh: 天都、臨羌砦戍守各以三千人爲額，仍各置馬軍蕃落、步軍保捷。

translations.literal: Tiandu and Linqiang stockades each fixed garrison at three thousand, each also establishing cavalry Tribal Frontier and infantry Secure Swift.
translations.idiomatic: Tiandu and Linqiang stockades each received a garrison quota of three thousand, with Tribal Frontier cavalry and Secure Swift infantry.

sentences.zh: 永興軍等路創置蕃落；

translations.literal: Yongxing Army and other circuits newly established Tribal Frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing Army and other circuits newly established Tribal Frontier units;

sentences.zh: 河北大名府等二十二州共創置馬軍廣威、步軍保捷，以河北大水，招刺流民故也。

translations.literal: twenty-two prefectures including Daming Prefecture in Hebei jointly established cavalry Broad Awesome and infantry Secure Swift, because of great floods in Hebei and recruitment of displaced refugees.
translations.idiomatic: and twenty-two Hebei prefectures including Daming established Broad Awesome cavalry and Secure Swift infantry to recruit refugees after severe flooding.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，環慶增置敢勇二百人。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Huanqing added two hundred Daring Valor troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 2, Huanqing added two hundred Daring Valor troops.

sentences.zh: 四月，環慶路都總管司言：「本路新展定邊城，比之橫山、興平等處城砦尤深，乞增置住營馬軍蕃落、步軍保捷。」

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the Huanqing Circuit supreme commander reported: 'This circuit has newly expanded Dingbian City; compared with Hengshan, Xingping, and other fortress stockades it lies deeper in hostile territory—we request addition of stationed cavalry Tribal Frontier and infantry Secure Swift.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, the Huanqing route commander reported, 'Our newly expanded Dingbian City lies deeper in hostile territory than Hengshan, Xingping, and other frontier posts. We request stationed Tribal Frontier cavalry and Secure Swift infantry.'

sentences.zh: 六月，環慶路都總管司言：「展築慶州白豹城，合增置住營馬步軍。」

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Huanqing Circuit supreme commander reported: 'In expanding Baibao City in Qingzhou, stationed cavalry and infantry should be added.'
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the Huanqing commander reported, 'Expansion of Baibao City in Qingzhou requires additional stationed cavalry and infantry.'

sentences.zh: 又鄜延路都總管司言：「本路新築米脂等八堡砦，合增置土兵、馬步軍。」

translations.literal: The Fuyan Circuit supreme commander also reported: 'This circuit has newly built eight fortress stockades including Mizhi—we request addition of local troops and cavalry and infantry.'
translations.idiomatic: The Fuyan commander also reported, 'Eight new stockades including Mizhi require additional local troops and cavalry and infantry.'

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All requests were approved.

sentences.zh: 三年，樞密院奏：「河北增置馬軍廣威、步軍保捷二萬餘人，欲令揀選升換在京闕額軍分。」

translations.literal: In the third year, the Bureau of Military Affairs reported: 'Hebei has added more than twenty thousand cavalry Broad Awesome and infantry Secure Swift; we wish to have them selected and promoted to fill vacant capital army slots.'
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, the Bureau of Military Affairs reported, 'Hebei has added more than twenty thousand Broad Awesome cavalry and Secure Swift infantry. We propose selecting the best to fill vacant capital army positions.'

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 自紹聖以來，陝西、河東連用兵六年，進築未已，覆軍殺將，供給不可勝紀。

translations.literal: From Shaosheng onward, Shaanxi and Hedong were at war continuously for six years; forward fortification did not cease; armies were destroyed and generals killed; supplies were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: From the Shaosheng era onward, Shaanxi and Hedong saw six years of continuous warfare. Forward fortification never stopped; armies were wiped out and generals killed; the cost of supply was incalculable.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月，廣西路置刀牌手三千人，於切要州軍更戌，以寧海名。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, Guangxi Circuit established three thousand saber-shield men, rotating garrison at critical prefectures and armies, under the name Secure Sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 4, Guangxi Circuit established three thousand saber-and-shield troops, rotated among critical prefectures, under the name Secure Sea.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔：「四輔屏翰京師，兵力不可偏重，可各以二萬人爲額。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict ordered: 'The four auxiliary prefectures that screen the capital must not have disproportionate military strength; each may be fixed at twenty thousand as quota.'
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, an edict declared, 'The four auxiliary prefectures guarding the capital must not hold disproportionate forces. Each is capped at twenty thousand men.'

sentences.zh: 五年，環慶路進築徐丁台城，賜名安邊，置馬軍蕃落、步軍保捷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Huanqing Circuit advanced construction of Xudingtai City, granted the name Secure Border, establishing cavalry Tribal Frontier and infantry Secure Swift.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, Huanqing built Xudingtai City, renamed Secure Border, and stationed Tribal Frontier cavalry and Secure Swift infantry there.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，詔；

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, an edict;
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang 1, an edict declared:

sentences.zh: 「廣西宜、融二州實爲極邊，舊置馬軍難議減省，且依元降指揮招置。」

translations.literal: 'Guangxi's Yi and Rong prefectures are truly on the extreme frontier; the cavalry long established there cannot easily be reduced—we order recruitment to continue as in the original directive.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Yi and Rong prefectures in Guangxi lie on the extreme frontier. Their established cavalry cannot readily be cut. Continue recruitment as in the original directive.'

sentences.zh: 自元豐而後，民兵日盛，募兵日衰，其募兵闕額，則收其廩給，以爲民兵教閱之費。

translations.literal: From Yuanfeng onward, militia grew daily stronger while recruited troops grew daily weaker; when recruited troops had vacant quotas, their rations were collected for militia drill expenses.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanfeng, militia grew stronger as recruited armies weakened. Vacant quotas in recruited units had their pay diverted to fund militia drill.

sentences.zh: 元祐以降，民兵亦衰。

translations.literal: From Yuanyou downward, militia also declined.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yuanyou era onward, the militia declined as well.

sentences.zh: 崇甯、大觀以來，蔡京用事，兵弊日滋，至於受逃亡，收配隸，猶恐不足。

translations.literal: From Chongning and Daguan onward, with Cai Jing in power, military abuses grew daily, until they accepted fugitives and enrolled convicts—still fearing insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongning and Daguan, with Cai Jing in power, military abuses worsened until the army accepted fugitives and convicts and still could not fill its ranks.

sentences.zh: 政和之後，久廢蒐補，軍士死亡之余，老疾者徒費廩給，少健者又多冗占，階級既壞，紀律遂亡。

translations.literal: After Zhenghe, search and replenishment were long abandoned; of soldiers beyond the dead, the old and ill merely wasted rations, the young and fit were mostly redundant placeholders—ranks ruined, discipline perished.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenghe, recruitment and replenishment ceased. The dead were not replaced; the old and sick wasted pay while the young and fit held redundant posts. Ranks collapsed and discipline died.

sentences.zh: 童貫握兵，勢傾內外，凡遇陣敗，恥於人言，第申逃竄。

translations.literal: Tong Guan held military power, his influence overwhelming inner and outer court; whenever defeated in battle, shamed before others' words, he merely reported flight and dispersal.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan held military power with influence over the whole court. After every defeat, ashamed to admit it, he reported only that troops had fled.

sentences.zh: 河北將兵，十無二三，往往多住招闕額，以其封樁爲上供之用。

translations.literal: Hebei general-command troops were two or three in ten at most; often many held recruitment vacancies, using sealed reserves for tribute to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei general-command forces were at most two or three tenths of their paper strength. Commanders kept vacancies on the rolls and diverted sealed funds to court tribute.

sentences.zh: 陝右諸路兵亦無幾，種師道將兵入援，止得萬五千人。

translations.literal: Troops in the Shaanxi right circuits were also few; when Zhong Shidao led troops to reinforce the capital, he obtained only fifteen thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Forces in the western Shaanxi circuits were equally few. When Zhong Shidao marched to the capital's relief, he mustered only fifteen thousand men.

sentences.zh: 故靖康之變，雖畫一之詔，哀痛激切，而事已無及矣。

translations.literal: Thus at the Jingkang crisis, though uniform edicts were issued, grief-stricken and urgent, the affair was already beyond remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the Jingkang disaster struck, even the court's anguished, sweeping edicts came too late.

sentences.zh: 高宗南渡，始建御營司，未幾，復並御營歸樞密院。

translations.literal: When Gaozong crossed south, the Imperial Camp Bureau was first established; before long it was merged back into the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong fled south, an Imperial Camp Bureau was established, then soon merged back into the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，改御前五軍爲神武軍，御營五軍爲神武副軍，並隸樞密院。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan, the five armies before the throne were changed to Divine Martial Army, the five Imperial Camp armies to Divine Martial Subsidiary Army—all subordinate to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 4, the five imperial guard armies became the Divine Martial Army and the five Imperial Camp armies the Divine Martial Subsidiary Army, both under the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 五年，上以祖宗故事，兵皆隸三衙，乃廢神武中軍隸殿前司，於是殿司兵柄始一。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the emperor, following ancestral precedent that all troops belonged to the Three Commands, abolished the Divine Martial central army and attached it to the Palace Front Bureau—thus the Palace Bureau's military authority was unified at last.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, citing ancestral precedent that all troops belonged to the Three Commands, the emperor abolished the Divine Martial central army and attached it to the Palace Front Bureau, unifying command under the Palace Bureau for the first time.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，詔殿前兵馬權以七萬三千人爲額。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao, an edict fixed Palace Front cavalry and infantry provisionally at 73,000 as quota.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 1, Palace Front cavalry and infantry were capped at 73,000.

sentences.zh: 諸屯駐大軍則皆諸將之部曲，高宗開元帥府，諸將兵悉隸焉。

translations.literal: The various encamped great armies were all the personal followings of generals; Gaozong opened marshal headquarters, and all generals' troops were subordinate thereto.
translations.idiomatic: The great encamped armies were the personal followings of individual generals. Gaozong established marshal headquarters, and all generals' troops fell under it.

sentences.zh: 建炎後，諸大將兵浸盛，因時制變，屯無常所。

translations.literal: After Jianyan, the great generals' armies gradually grew powerful; adapting to circumstances, encampments had no fixed place.
translations.idiomatic: After Jianyan, the great generals' armies grew powerful and shifted camp according to circumstance, with no fixed stations.

sentences.zh: 如劉光世軍或在鎮江、池州、太平，韓世忠軍或屯江州、江陰，岳飛一軍或屯宜興、蔣山，王彥八字軍隨張浚入蜀，吳玠兵多屯鳳州、大散關、和尚原。

translations.literal: For example, Liu Guangshi's army might be at Zhenjiang, Chizhou, or Taiping; Han Shizhong's at Jiangzhou or Jiangyin; Yue Fei's single army at Yixing or Jiangshan; Wang Yan's Eight-Character Army followed Zhang Jun into Shu; Wu Jie's troops mostly encamped at Fengzhou, Dasan Pass, and Heshang Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi's army might be at Zhenjiang, Chizhou, or Taiping; Han Shizhong's at Jiangzhou or Jiangyin; Yue Fei's at Yixing or Jiangshan; Wang Yan's Eight-Character Army followed Zhang Jun into Shu; Wu Jie's mostly held Fengzhou, Dasan Pass, and Heshang Plain.

sentences.zh: 是時合內外大軍十九萬四千餘，川、陝不與焉。

translations.literal: At that time inner and outer great armies combined totaled more than 194,000—Sichuan and Shaanxi not included.
translations.idiomatic: At that time armies inside and outside the capital totaled more than 194,000, not counting Sichuan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 及楊沂中將中軍總宿衛，江東劉光世、淮東韓世忠、湖北岳飛、湖南王𤫉四軍共十九萬一千六百，亦未嘗有屯。

translations.literal: When Yang Yizhong commanded the central army for palace guard duty overall, the four armies of Jiangdong Liu Guangshi, Huaidong Han Shizhong, Hubei Yue Fei, and Hunan Wang Yuan totaled 191,600—yet they too had no fixed encampments.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yizhong commanded the central army as overall palace guard, the four armies of Liu Guangshi in Jiangdong, Han Shizhong in Huaidong, Yue Fei in Hubei, and Wang Yuan in Hunan totaled 191,600—yet they too had no fixed stations.

sentences.zh: 紹興十一年，范同以諸將握兵難制，獻謀秦檜，且以柘皋之捷言於上，召張俊、韓世忠、岳飛入覲，張俊首納所部兵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shaoxing, Fan Tong, because the generals holding troops were hard to control, offered counsel to Qin Hui and also spoke to the emperor of the victory at Zhegao; Zhang Jun, Han Shizhong, and Yue Fei were summoned to audience; Zhang Jun was first to submit his troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 11, Fan Tong urged Qin Hui that the generals' private armies were hard to control, cited the victory at Zhegao to the emperor, and had Zhang Jun, Han Shizhong, and Yue Fei summoned to court. Zhang Jun was the first to surrender his command.

sentences.zh: 分命三大帥副校各統所部，自爲一軍，更銜曰統制御前軍馬。

translations.literal: The three great commanders' deputy commanders were separately ordered each to command his own division as an independent army, with the new title Controller of Armies and Horses Before the Throne.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commanders under the three great marshals were each ordered to lead his own force as a separate army under the new title Controller of Armies and Horses Before the Throne.

sentences.zh: 罷宣撫司，遇出師取旨，兵皆隸樞密院，屯駐仍舊。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commission was abolished; when troops went out on campaign they took orders from court; all armies were subordinate to the Bureau of Military Affairs, encampments remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Commission was abolished. Campaigns required court approval; all troops fell under the Bureau of Military Affairs, though garrisons stayed where they were.

sentences.zh: 而四川大將兵曰興、成、階、鳳、文、龍、利、閬、金、洋、綿、房、西和州、大安軍、興元、隆慶、潼川府凡十七郡，亦分屯就糧焉。

translations.literal: Sichuan's great general-command troops garrisoned seventeen prefectures in all—Xing, Cheng, Jie, Feng, Wen, Long, Li, Lang, Jin, Yang, Mian, Fang, Xihe Prefecture, Da'an Army, Xingyuan, Longqing, and Tongchuan Prefecture—also distributed in grain-supplied encampments.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan's great armies garrisoned seventeen jurisdictions—Xing, Cheng, Jie, Feng, Wen, Long, Li, Lang, Jin, Yang, Mian, Fang, Xihe, Da'an, Xingyuan, Longqing, and Tongchuan—also on local grain-supply stations.

sentences.zh: 乾道之末，各州有都統司領兵：建康五萬，池州一萬二千，鎮江四萬七千，楚州武鋒軍一萬一千，鄂州四萬九千，荊南二萬，興元一萬七千，金州一萬一千。

translations.literal: At the end of Qiandao, each prefecture had a supreme command office leading troops: Jiankang 50,000, Chizhou 12,000, Zhenjiang 47,000, Chuzhou Martial Edge Army 11,000, Ezhou 49,000, Jingnan 20,000, Xingyuan 17,000, Jinzhou 11,000.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Qiandao, supreme command offices led troops at: Jiankang 50,000, Chizhou 12,000, Zhenjiang 47,000, Chuzhou Martial Edge Army 11,000, Ezhou 49,000, Jingnan 20,000, Xingyuan 17,000, and Jinzhou 11,000.

sentences.zh: 其後分屯列戍，增損靡常。

translations.literal: Later, distributed encampments and frontier garrisons increased and decreased without fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: Later garrisons were distributed along the frontier with strengths that changed constantly.

sentences.zh: 所可考者，統制、統領、正將、副將、準備將之目也。

translations.literal: What can be verified are the categories of controller, commander, chief officer, deputy officer, and ready officer.
translations.idiomatic: What can be verified are the ranks of controller, commander, chief officer, deputy officer, and ready officer.

sentences.zh: 至於水軍之制，則有加于前者，南渡以後，江、淮皆爲邊境故也。

translations.literal: As for the naval system, it exceeded what came before, because after the southern crossing the Yangzi and Huai became frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: The navy exceeded earlier systems because after the flight south the Yangzi and Huai had become frontiers.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，李綱請於沿江、淮、河帥府置水兵二軍，要郡別置水兵一軍，次要郡別置中軍，招善舟楫者充，立軍號曰淩波、樓船軍。

translations.literal: Early in Jianyan, Li Gang requested that along the Yangzi, Huai, and Yellow River marshal prefectures two naval armies be established; key prefectures each one naval army; secondary prefectures each a middle army—recruiting those skilled in boats, with army designations Wave-Cleaving and Tower Ship.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyan, Li Gang proposed two naval armies along the Yangzi, Huai, and Yellow River, one naval army in each key prefecture, and a middle army in lesser prefectures, recruiting skilled boatmen under the names Wave-Cleaving and Tower Ship.

sentences.zh: 其戰艦則有海鰍、水哨馬、雙車、得勝、十棹、大飛、旗捷、防沙、平底、水飛馬之名。

translations.literal: Their warships bore the names Sea Mackerel, Water Courier Horse, Double Cart, Victor, Ten Oars, Great Flyer, Banner Swift, Sand Guard, Flat Bottom, and Water Flying Horse.
translations.idiomatic: Warships included the Sea Mackerel, Water Courier Horse, Double Cart, Victor, Ten Oars, Great Flyer, Banner Swift, Sand Guard, Flat Bottom, and Water Flying Horse types.

sentences.zh: 隆興以後至於寶祐、景定間，江、淮沿流堡隘相望，守禦益繁，民勞益甚。

translations.literal: From Longxing onward through Baoyou and Jingding, along the Yangzi and Huai fortress passes faced one another in succession; defense grew ever more elaborate, the people's labor ever heavier.
translations.idiomatic: From Longxing through Baoyou and Jingding, fortresses lined the Yangzi and Huai. Defense grew ever more elaborate and the people's burden ever heavier.

sentences.zh: 迨鹹淳末，廣東籍蜑丁，閩海拘舶船民船，公私俱弊矣。

translations.literal: By the end of Xianchun, Guangdong registered Tanka boat people, Fujian seas seized merchant and civilian vessels—public and private alike were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Xianchun, Guangdong registered Tanka boat people and Fujian seized merchant and civilian vessels—ruining both state and people.

sentences.zh: 其禁軍將校，則有殿前司都指揮使、副都指揮使、都虞候各一人；

translations.literal: Palace Army officers and NCOs included: Palace Front Bureau commander-in-chief, deputy commander-in-chief, and chief adjutant, one each;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Army officers included a commander-in-chief, deputy commander-in-chief, and chief adjutant for the Palace Front Bureau, one of each;

sentences.zh: 諸班有都虞候、指揮使、都知、副都知、押班；

translations.literal: the various units had chief adjutant, commander, chief knower, deputy chief knower, and escort chief;
translations.idiomatic: direct units had chief adjutant, commander, chief knower, deputy chief knower, and escort chief;

sentences.zh: 御龍諸直有四直都虞候，本直各有都虞候、指揮使、副指揮使、都頭、副都頭、十將、將虞候；

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon Direct units had four Direct chief adjutants; each Direct had chief adjutant, commander, deputy commander, squad chief, deputy squad chief, ten-man leader, and adjutant NCO;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Dragon Direct units had four Direct chief adjutants; each Direct had chief adjutant, commander, deputy commander, squad chief, deputy squad chief, ten-man leader, and adjutant NCO;

sentences.zh: 馬步軍有捧日、天武左右四廂都指揮使，捧日、天武左右各有都指揮使，每軍有都指揮使、都虞候，每指揮有指揮使、副指揮使，每都有軍使、步軍謂之都頭。

translations.literal: cavalry and infantry had left and right Sun-Holding and Heavenly Martial four-wing commanders-in-chief; Sun-Holding and Heavenly Martial left and right each had commanders-in-chief; each army had commander-in-chief and chief adjutant; each command had commander and deputy commander; each company had army envoy—in infantry called squad chief.
translations.idiomatic: cavalry and infantry had four-wing commanders-in-chief for Sun-Holding and Heavenly Martial left and right; each wing had its commander-in-chief; each army had commander-in-chief and chief adjutant; each command had commander and deputy; each company had an army envoy—in infantry called squad chief.

sentences.zh: 副兵馬使、步軍謂之副都頭。

translations.literal: Deputy horse-army envoy—in infantry called deputy squad chief.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy horse-army envoy—in infantry, deputy squad chief.

sentences.zh: 十將、將虞候、承局、押官。

translations.literal: Ten-man leader, adjutant NCO, clerk, and escort officer.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-man leader, adjutant NCO, clerk, and escort officer.

sentences.zh: 所領諸班直、指揮，騎兵、步兵之額敘列如左。

translations.literal: The strengths of Direct Units, commands, cavalry, and infantry under their command are set forth below.
translations.idiomatic: The strengths of the Direct Units, commands, cavalry, and infantry under their command are set forth below.

sentences.zh: 以其前後之異同者分爲建隆以來之制、熙寧以後之制，而將兵、水兵之制可考者，因附著於後雲。

translations.literal: Because of differences before and after, these are divided into the system from Jianlong onward and the system from Xining onward; what can be verified of general-command and naval systems is appended below.
translations.idiomatic: Differences before and after are treated under systems from Jianlong onward and from Xining onward; verifiable information on general-command and naval forces is appended below.

sentences.zh: 建隆以來之制

translations.literal: The System from Jianlong Onward
translations.idiomatic: The System from Jianlong Onward

sentences.zh: 殿前指揮使左右班二。

translations.literal: Palace Front Commander, left and right units, two.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Front Commander, left and right units: two.

sentences.zh: 宋初，以舊府親從帶甲之士及諸班軍騎中選武藝絕倫者充。

translations.literal: Early in Song, chosen from the old prefecture's armored personal followers and from cavalry of the various units—those of peerless martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, they were chosen from the old prefecture's armored personal followers and from unit cavalry for peerless martial skill.

sentences.zh: 內殿直左右班四。

translations.literal: Inner Palace Direct, left and right units, four.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Palace Direct, left and right units: four.

sentences.zh: 周制，簡軍校暨武臣子弟有材勇者立。

translations.literal: Zhou system: selected from army officers and martial officials' sons—those of talent and courage were established.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou system, they were drawn from army officers and martial officials' sons of talent and courage.

sentences.zh: 又有川班內殿直，乾德三年平蜀得奇兵，簡閱材貌魁偉便習騎射者凡百二十人立，開寶四年廢。

translations.literal: There was also Sichuan-unit Inner Palace Direct: in the third year of Qiande, pacifying Shu yielded exceptional troops; one hundred twenty men of imposing stature skilled in mounted archery were selected and established—abolished in the fourth year of Kaibao.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Sichuan Inner Palace Direct unit: in Qiande 3, pacification of Shu yielded exceptional troops, and 120 men of imposing stature skilled in mounted archery were selected—abolished in Kaibao 4.

sentences.zh: 散員左右班四。

translations.literal: Dispersed Attendants, left and right units, four.
translations.idiomatic: Dispersed Attendants, left and right units: four.

sentences.zh: 周制，招置諸州豪傑立，散指揮、散都頭、散祗候凡十二班。

translations.literal: Zhou system: recruited and established heroes from various prefectures; Dispersed Commanders, Dispersed Squad Chiefs, and Dispersed Palace Attendants totaled twelve units.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou system, heroes from various prefectures were recruited; Dispersed Commanders, Dispersed Squad Chiefs, and Dispersed Palace Attendants totaled twelve units.

sentences.zh: 又於北面驍捷員僚直及諸軍內簡閱填補。
